tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.inHouse: Colourless, pale yellow or pale greenish-yellow liquid. Characteristic odour and taste followed by a sensation of cold.

tests.procedure: Miscible 10 mL of sample with ethanol and with methylene chloride.

Relative density by pycnometer: weigh the dry empty pycnometer (W1); fill with water and weigh (W2); fill with sample and weigh (W3). Weight of water W4 = W2 - W1; weight of sample W5 = W3 - W1; relative density = W5 / W4.

details.verificationReport: Analytical method verification report for relative density in Mint Flavor

tests.procedure: Transfer the sample to the prism of a calibrated refractometer and read the refractive index on the scale.

details.verificationReport: Analytical method verification report for refractive index in Mint Flavor

tests.procedure: Using a calibrated polarimeter: set the zero with the empty tube, fill with sample and detect the angle of rotation.

details.verificationReport: Analytical method verification report for optical rotation in Mint Flavor

tests.procedure: Acid value: dissolve about 5.00 g (W) of sample in 50 mL of a mixture of equal volumes of ethanol (96 %) and light petroleum, previously neutralised with 0.1 M potassium hydroxide or 0.1 M sodium hydroxide. Add 0.5 mL phenolphthalein solution R1 as indicator; titrate with 0.1 M potassium hydroxide or 0.1 M sodium hydroxide until the pink colour persists for at least 15 s (n mL of titrant). Acid value = 5.61 x n / W.

details.solvent: 50 mL ethanol (96 %) : light petroleum, equal volumes
details.titrant: 0.1 M potassium hydroxide or 0.1 M sodium hydroxide
details.endpoint: pink colour persists at least 15 s
details.verificationReport: Analytical method verification report for acid value in Mint Flavor

tests.procedure: Microbial enumeration per USP <2021>, membrane filtration: suspend 10 mL sample in SCDB to 100 mL; filter the dilution (equivalent to 0.1 mL of sample) through a 0.45 µm membrane, wash with phosphate buffer pH 7.2 (three 100 mL volumes, repeated); place membranes on SCDA (TAMC, 24-72 h at 30-35 °C) and SDA (TYMC, 5-7 days at 20-25 °C). Count colonies, average the plates and calculate CFU/ml x DF (DF = 10).
Yeasts and molds, same membrane filtration as TAMC; SDA plates incubated 5-7 days at 20-25 °C; average the two SDA plates and calculate CFU/ml x DF (DF = 10).

Specified microorganism E. coli per USP 2024 <2022>: filter 10 mL sample dilution in SCDB, incubate SCDB 30-35 °C 24-48 h; transfer 1 mL to MacConkey broth (MBP), 42-44 °C 24-48 h; subculture on MacConkey agar (MAR) 30-35 °C 18-24 h; confirm by Gram stain, EMB and TBX (42-44 °C 18-72 h) and optionally an identification system (probability above 70 %).

Specified microorganism Salmonella spp.: from the incubated SCDB (18-24 h at 30-35 °C), transfer 1 mL to RVS broth, 30-35 °C 18-24 h; streak on XLD, BGA or HEA, 30-35 °C 24-48 h; confirm by Gram stain and TSI slant (red alkaline slope, yellow acid butt) and optionally a biochemical identification system (probability above 70 %).

details.media: SCDB, RVS, XLD, BGA, HEA, TSI

openQuestions.question: The STM marks the microbiological tests (TAMC, TYMC, E. coli, Salmonella) 'Only for the Natural Origin mint', but the spec sheet lists them with no such qualifier. Confirm which mint grades they apply to.

Optical rotation: the STM and spec state an angle of rotation (-30° to -10°) with no sample concentration or path length, so this is not a specific rotation. Recorded as optical rotation (observed angle).
